subject: Mobile Development
title: Paid Apps: A Dying Breed
description: A quick, practical guide to Paid Apps: A Dying Breed.

hook.text: In 2009, most apps cost $0.99 or more. Today, over 95% of app downloads are free.

buildup.text: Users expect apps to be free. Charging upfront dramatically reduces download numbers.

discovery.text: Paid apps still exist in niches — productivity tools, pro utilities, and premium games.

twist.text: Some developers returned to paid models to escape the ad-tracking and data-harvesting cycle.

climax.text: The paid app model isn't dead, but it's reserved for users willing to pay for quality.

punchline.text: Free won the market, but paid survived in niches.

quiz.question: Why did paid apps decline?
options: Users expect free apps, reducing downloads for paid ones
